answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence shared decisions. A new identity then adds no weight unless it commits real capital; if it signs conflicting attestations, the protocol destroys part of that stake. This makes an attack costly in proportion to its voting power and duration, while honest agents can recover funds. The terrace, knoll, and ember labels might organize groups, but none substitutes for the bonded stake.
